item.title: Whale genome decoded using drone and whale snot
item.description: Scientists have for the first time mapped a whale's complete genome using snot. Marine mammal ecologist Éadin O'Mahony and colleagues used small commercial drones with sterile petri dishes attached to capture the exhaled water vapor from whales. item.description: Grand Theft Auto VI, the latest game from Rockstar Games, has been released and breaks with the franchise's hypermasculine reputation. For the first time, a female protagonist, Lucia Caminos, is not optional: she forms a criminal and romantic duo with Jason Duval. item.title: Red dress embroidered by 380 women from 51 countries
item.description: Textile artist Kirstie Macleod conceived the Red Dress project in 2009: a dress made of 87 pieces of burgundy silk that travelled the world to be embroidered. Over 14 years, 380 people from 51 countries worked on it, including 141 paid craftswomen and the rest volunteers. item.description: Christian Ogley, owner of Blind Jack's pub in Knaresborough, England, has spent approximately 6,000 dollars on an impressive Christmas light display to brighten the local community after a difficult year marked by rising cost of living. item.title: Drone captures whale breath for genome research without disruption
item.description: Researchers from the University of St. Andrews were part of an international team that for the first time sequenced a complete whale genome based on exhaled breath collected with a small drone. Earlier methods used darts and biopsies that disturbed the animals. The team attached sterile petri dishes to a drone and collected 58 breath samples from 26 humpback whales...

item.description: In the South Korean city of Chuncheon, schools are experimenting with the 'Great Books' educational model from St. John's College in the US. Students read classic texts, such as Frankenstein, and debate them without the help of the internet or AI chatbots. Teachers do not lecture but only facilitate discussion. item.description: Since 2021, chef Maddy Goldberg has been cooking 100 hot meals every Tuesday for visitors to the Fort York Food Bank in Toronto. item.description: The Ora-pro-nobis, a thorny climbing plant, offers a fresh perspective on vegetable gardening thanks to its exceptional nutritional value. Brazilian laboratories analyzed the leaves and found approximately 22% protein on a dry matter basis, or roughly 2 grams of protein per 100 grams of fresh product — more than most traditional leafy vegetables. item.title: Algae diet makes wild fish unnecessary in fish farming
item.description: Researchers at the University of California Santa Cruz have developed a fully algae-based feed for farmed fish that could make wild fish redundant in fish feed. Farmed salmon and trout are currently often fed wild-caught sardines, herring, anchovies or mackerel, which contributes to overfishing. item.description: Every Tuesday, chef Maddy Goldberg from Toronto prepares a meal for a hundred people in need, made from random ingredients she finds at the local food bank. item.description: In Assam, India, father and daughter Mahesh Chandra Bora and Nisha Bora founded Elrhino Stationery, a company that makes paper from the dung of rhinoceroses and elephants. The idea emerged after Mahesh read about similar paper production in Rajasthan. item.title: Son tracks down writers of comfort letters to wounded Vietnam veteran
item.description: In 1967, 33 schoolchildren from Massachusetts wrote letters to Navy corpsman Russell Jacobson, who had suffered 12 gunshot wounds and shrapnel injuries in Vietnam. Severely wounded and unable to speak, he lay in Chelsea Naval Hospital, where he refused food and water. The letters, organized by a nun through St. Ann School in Gloucester, helped him recover. item.description: A hollow or rotting tree in the garden may look like dead wood, but it actually provides a valuable refuge for wildlife. In autumn, bats, which feed primarily on insects, actively search for food to build up fat reserves for hibernation. item.description: Audrey Hepburn was known for her classic beauty and accepted aging with grace. She always rejected plastic surgery and was proud of her wrinkles. item.description: Many people unknowingly have a small nature reserve in their backyard, with birds such as robins, house sparrows, cardinals, jays and tits. item.description: The courage of British shopkeeper Ada Le Poidevin, who hid three British soldiers on Nazi-occupied Guernsey during the Second World War, has come to light forty years after her death. Her 79-year-old niece Liz Walton uncovered the story thanks to photographs, diaries and data from Ancestry.com. item.description: A cell therapy originally developed against cancer is proving helpful for stiff person syndrome, a rare autoimmune disease in which the immune system attacks the central nervous system. item.description: Chester Zoo was the only zoo in Europe this year to successfully hatch a Malaysian peacock pheasant. Only 15 of these endangered birds are being raised in captivity across European zoos.
